title: Python slot claim: mode (key 3) accepts CBOR bool/float via == equality — signed-claim divergence vs Rust uint()
description: Codereview finding (s61e security pass, reviewer kimi-k3), verified against cbor2 decode behavior. python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py:281-286: 'mode == _MODE_INTERLEAVED' / '== _MODE_CONTIGUOUS' uses value equality — False == 0, True == 1, 0.0 == 0, 1.0 == 1 all hold, and cbor2 decodes CBOR false/true/float-0/float-1 to exactly those Python values. A wire claim with key 3 = 0xf4 (false) is accepted as INTERLEAVED by Python; Rust decodes mode via p.uint() (slot.rs:580) and rejects non-uint major types as MalformedClaim. Exploitable with a valid signature: a malicious federation gateway signs the canonical payload (mode=0), flips the mode byte on the wire; verify_slot_claim re-encodes via encode_claim_canonical (int 0), digest matches, Python accepts, Rust rejects — the same divergence class jkuj/s61e closed for keys 1/2/4/6/7. Fix: 'if type(mode) is not int or mode not in (_MODE_INTERLEAVED, _MODE_CONTIGUOUS): raise ClaimError' (type() is int also excludes bool). Pin with a decode test: tamper key 3 to False/0.0 on the happy_path_n1 envelope (same pattern as test_oversized_sibling_fields_rejected_at_decode).
close_reason: Already landed at HEAD via sync daemon (commit 916eec0ed9, per Mark's comment on the bead). Verified: slot_claim.py:306 has 'type(mode) is not int or mode not in (...)' type-strict decode; test_slot_claim_cose_vectors.py:203-207 pins with bad_mode parametrize [False, True, 0.0, 1.0, 2, None, '0']. Test run: 96 passed, 3 skipped (gateway slot_claim suites). No duplicate work needed.
